title: Richard Henderson
summary: In 1775 Richard Henderson’s Transylvania Company bargained with Cherokee headmen at Sycamore Shoals for about 20 million acres of Kentucky land.
bodyMarkdown:
Richard Henderson was a North Carolina judge and land speculator who tried to turn much of Kentucky into a private colony. His 1775 purchase from Cherokee leaders opened the way for Boonesborough and the Wilderness Road. It also deepened a split within the Cherokee Nation and was later voided by Virginia.

## Judge and speculator

The [Wikipedia article on Henderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Henderson_%28jurist%29) says he was born in Hanover County, Virginia, on April 20, 1735, and grew up in Granville County, North Carolina. He studied law and was appointed a judge of the Superior Court in 1768. He retired from the bench in 1773 to pursue land deals.

On August 27, 1774, Henderson organized a land company with other prominent North Carolinians. It was first called Richard Henderson and Company, then the Louisa Company. On January 6, 1775, it became the Transylvania Company.

## Sycamore Shoals

In March 1775 Henderson met more than 1,200 Cherokee at Sycamore Shoals, in present Elizabethton, Tennessee, according to the [Wikipedia article on the Treaty of Sycamore Shoals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Sycamore_Shoals). Leaders including Attakullakulla and Oconostota were present. The [Grokipedia article on Henderson](https://grokipedia.com/page/Richard_Henderson_%28jurist%29) dates the treaty to March 17 and says the company acquired roughly 20 million acres in present Kentucky and Tennessee. The Cherokee received trade goods valued at about £10,000, including guns, ammunition, cloth and tools.

Not all Cherokee accepted the sale. Attakullakulla's son, the war leader [Dragging Canoe](https://grokipedia.com/page/Dragging_Canoe), refused to sign. Wikipedia quotes his warning that "it is bloody ground, and will be dark and difficult to settle." He led his followers south toward present Chattanooga, and they became the [Chickamauga Cherokee](/stories/chickamauga-cherokee/), who resisted settlement for years.

## A colony that failed

Henderson hired Daniel Boone to blaze the Wilderness Road through Cumberland Gap into the purchase. Boone's party founded Boonesborough, where [Richard Callaway](/stories/col-richard-callaway-of-boonesborough/) became a leader. In May 1775 settlers there drafted the Transylvania Compact under a large elm, planning executive, legislative and judicial branches. Henderson then asked Congress to recognize Transylvania as a fourteenth colony, but Congress would not act without Virginia and North Carolina, which both claimed the land.

In June 1776 Virginia barred the company from making demands on settlers, and in December 1778 it declared the claim void. North Carolina voided the Tennessee part in 1783. Henderson and his partners received 200,000 acres on the Ohio River below the mouth of the Green River instead. In 1779–80 Henderson also backed the settlement of the Cumberland Valley, where James Robertson and John Donelson led the parties that built Fort Nashborough, the start of Nashville.

## Kentucky today

Henderson died in North Carolina on January 30, 1785. A settlement at Red Banks on his company's Ohio River grant became the town of Henderson in 1797, and Henderson County was later named for him. The story of that town is told in [Henderson at Red Banks](/stories/henderson-at-red-banks/).
